title: Productized design-source home + locked in-code target reference — prior art (Figma freeze · design tokens · locked visual baselines · perceptual oracle · interaction tests)
summary: Prep research for decision #2801 (under UI-Fidelity Gate epic #2804; extends target-registry slice #2806). The UI-Fidelity Gate's RRFC INVARIANT A locks every UI story to a registry-anchored, content-hashed design target so a perceptual-distance oracle holds; today that target is a throwaway claude.ai artifact link. This surveys how to PRODUCTIZE the design-source home and the locked in-code target. BOTTOM LINE — the cross-industry pattern is FREEZE-TO-AN-IN-REPO-ARTIFACT (design tokens JSON, or a committed accepted image) that is content-keyed and diffed by a threshold oracle; you NEVER point the oracle at a live URL. FIGMA REST: GET /v1/files/:key (and /nodes) accept a ?version=<id> param that pins an immutable historical state; GET /v1/images/:key renders a node to an image (format/scale/version) but returns an EPHEMERAL Figma-CDN URL (community-reported ~30-day expiry) so you must download the bytes; GET /v1/files/:key/versions lists named versions {id, created_at, label, description, user}; webhooks v2 FILE_VERSION_UPDATE fires only when a NAMED version is created (the low-noise 'new locked candidate' trigger) vs FILE_UPDATE on every edit. Figma Dev Mode extracts visual props only (no structure/logic); Code Connect MAPS a Figma component to your real production component (CLI-published config in your repo), it does not generate code. DESIGN TOKENS: the W3C Design Tokens Community Group (DTCG) format ($value/$type/$description/$extensions) reached first stable v1 in Oct 2025; Style Dictionary v4 has first-class DTCG support (tokens JSON -> transforms -> platform outputs); Tokens Studio authors tokens in Figma and exports DTCG JSON / syncs to Git — the strongest 'design decision as a diffable, versioned, in-repo JSON artifact' model. LOCKED VISUAL BASELINES: Chromatic snapshots each story x viewport x browser x mode and diffs against an ACCEPTED baseline (Accept promotes; baselines are branch-scoped and promote to main on merge); diff is color-distance in YIQ space with a default threshold 0.063; TurboSnap keys off the Git dependency graph + commit SHA to re-snapshot only changed stories and copy unchanged baselines forward. Percy is the same approve-to-promote model (default baseline = latest approved build on the base branch). BOTH keep the baseline SERVER-SIDE (hosted, approvable) — jest-image-snapshot is the closer analog to our design: baseline PNGs COMMITTED in-repo under __image_snapshots__. CONTENT-ADDRESSING: Git is a content-addressable store (object id = sha1/sha256 over content) and package-lock 'integrity' hashes pin+verify a resolved artifact — our 'registry-anchored, content-hashed target' is the design-world lockfile entry {registryId, versionId, sha256(mockBytes)}. THE ORACLE (three tiers, layer them): pixelmatch (per-pixel YIQ distance + anti-alias detector + threshold) is deterministic but subpixel/font-hinting sensitive; SSIM (structural similarity, >0.99 ~ no visible change for UI) is a good perceptual-distance FLOOR; pHash (DCT->64-bit fingerprint, Hamming distance) is a cheap PRE-FILTER only, and is a PERCEPTUAL hash of the rendered image, DISTINCT from the CRYPTOGRAPHIC content hash that locks the mock bytes — you want both. VERSIONING/COMPARE UI: Figma version history (named checkpoints = pinnable units) and Figma Branching (Org/Enterprise: branch off main, review side-by-side/overlay, merge with an extra version checkpoint — the native 'author iterations then promote one'; Abstract pioneered this for Sketch/Figma and was largely absorbed). INTERACTIONS: Figma prototypes are ADVISORY by design — the REST API exposes some prototype metadata (prototypeStartNodeID, transitions) but NO first-class executable/assertable interaction contract; the CHECKABLE prior art is Storybook interaction tests (play() functions driving userEvent + asserting with expect from storybook/test, run in a real browser in CI) — i.e. transcribe an interaction into a real test, don't make the Figma prototype the checker. RECOMMENDATIONS FED TO #2801 (defaults sharpened by an adversarial skeptic + a fresh-context two-confusion screen): (Fork 1) the in-code artifact is the SOLE content-hashed canon; a rendered baseline is a NON-canonical, tolerance-compared product-repo artifact for the advisory perceptual layer — never a hashed co-anchor (a render is not byte-deterministic), never in WE; (Fork 2) normalize every source into ONE source-agnostic in-code artifact + provenance, AND archive the raw native payload (opaque, non-canonical) for lossless offline re-normalization; Figma is an importer that pins ?version and freezes the bytes; (Fork 3) the version-MINTING mechanism (id scheme + hash rule + append-only ledger + token-over-hash) is a minter-agnostic WE CONTRACT that any client calls — the design-studio #2676 is one minter-client (the human versioning UI folds there, product-internal, but does NOT own the identity contract); minting identity from a single product surface would lock out other minters; (Fork 4) cut interactions on ASSERTABILITY — gate deterministic post-interaction states (focus / aria-* flips / loading-error) NOW via the boolean floor (Storybook play-style post-event assertions folded into the existing webcase floor); motion/timing/prototype-feel stays advisory (mirrors ratified oracle-tightness B). Full grounding in we:reports/2026-08-01-design-source-home-locked-target.md.
